findings.claim: No test checks that a done task's bad due date or priority is ignored under --tag, although AC-6 says they are not checked at all except without --tag being irrelevant.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation that validates all tasks' due and priority whenever --tag is given would exit 2 on a file with a done task having due 'bad' under `stats --tag x`; every test still passes because the done-task due/priority case is only run in plain `stats`.
findings.evidence:
path = write(tmp_path, [t(1), t(2, True, due="bad", priority="urgent")])
    assert stats(path, capsys)[0] == 0

findings.claim: AC-6 'first offending task by id' is never tested with two offenders in the same field, so an implementation reporting the last (or any) offender passes.
findings.failure_scenario: File with open tasks 3 and 5 both having bad due dates: code that reports task 5 (e.g. iterating in reverse) passes all tests, since every test has only one offender per field.
